thread:
maria (support): customer 'AcmePayments' reporting intermittent TLS failures when their private VPC in eu-west calls our Private deployment in us-east. They see 'tls: handshake failure: remote error: tls: bad certificate'.

raj (sre): thanks — any repro steps or logs? is it consistently failing or only some requests?

maria (support): intermittent, seems location-dependent. They said requests from one AZ resolve to 10.2.x.x and others to public IP. When it hits the 10.2 internal IP we get the cert mismatch. Attached snippet from their curl: 

```curl -v https://inference.private.redwood.example/api/v1/generate
* Connected to inference.private.redwood.example (10.2.45.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using ...
* server certificate verification failed. CAfile: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt 
  CApath: /etc/ssl/certs
* SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name 'inference.private.redwood.example'
```

emma (neteng): that screams split-horizon / private hosted zone propagation or a stale DNScache returning internal endpoint that serves a cert for the node IP (not the SAN). Which DNS is the VPC using? Route53 resolver or custom dns?

maria (support): customer uses Route53 Resolver endpoints and has cross-account rules. They say flaps when hitting some subnets.

leo (solutions): can we confirm which IPs the certs are issued for? openssl s_client -connect ip:443 -servername inference.private.redwood.example will show cert CN/SAN. Maybe some node ended up with wrong cert (node identity rotated during a deploy).

raj (sre): good call. I asked the customer to run both:
```dig +short inference.private.redwood.example @<resolver-ip>
openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername inference.private.redwood.example -showcerts
```
They posted results: one AZ resolves to 10.2.45.12 (cert CN=node-45.redwood.internal), other AZ resolves to 10.3.12.9 (cert SAN includes inference.private.redwood.example).

emma (neteng): so two different backends. Hypothesis: Private hosted zone entry is correct (points to ELB internal DNS) but the resolver in one AZ is returning node IPs because of stale cache or because there's a Route53 inbound resolver rule resolving to an old IP from upstream. Another possibility: our internal autoscaling replaced an ALB with direct node targets in that AZ temporarily (bad rollout).

oncall-net (neteng): I'm looking at VPC endpoints and NACLs — nothing obvious. However, I see a stuck A record in a delegated private hosted zone for the customer's account that still points to a node IP (10.2.45.12). TTL was 300 but apparently cached in resolver.

ops-bot: Note: deployment 2026-03-15T02:17Z rolled hotfix 'node-cert-rotation' to us-east-1a, 1b. Canary passed but we reverted 2026-03-15T03:12Z for 1a only.

raj (sre): that revert timing aligns. If 1a served direct node IPs for a short window, some resolver caches might still return that address. Need to flush Route53 private zone and advise the customer to clear their resolver cache or restart their resolver endpoints. In the short term, we can add an nginx fronting that returns proper cert for bare hostnames, but prefer fixing DNS propagation.

maria (support): customer is asking for a mitigation because production traffic is affected. Any simple client-side workaround?

leo (solutions): tell them to set curl to use SNI and verify host (they already do), but the real workaround is to force resolution to the canonical internal ALB DNS by adding a static /etc/hosts entry — temporary and only for a few hosts — or route via our public edge (if allowed). Also recommend restart of their Route53 resolver endpoints to clear cache.

emma (neteng): action items: (1) neteng to clean up stuck A record in delegated private hosted zone (I've raised a ticket and will do immediate delete/replace) (2) sre to check any leftover node-targeted load balancers and ensure all backends present proper certs (raj) (3) advise customer to flush resolver cache / restart stub resolver or add hosts entry (maria/leo).

raj (sre): I'll also add a temporary rule to our firewall egress allowlist to force customer traffic through our secure egress proxy in us-east for 24h so connections terminate at a known-good cert.

maria (support): relayed plan to customer. They're going to restart resolvers and apply hosts on 2 affected app nodes, will report back in 30m. Thanks.

oncall-net (neteng): FYI after cleanup, I patched the private zone and forced propagation. Also cleared the resolver rule cache on the inbound resolver via API call.

maria (support): customer confirmed after restart: TLS errors dropped to 0 and requests normalize. They will keep monitoring. :relieved:

leo (solutions): please follow up with a postmortem — root cause looks like a partial rollback during cert-rotation deploy left a stale A record pointing to a node that presented node certs. Need deploy guardrails to avoid serving direct node IPs.

raj (sre): agreed. I'll open a postmortem with repro steps, logs (deploy timing), and suggested deployment checks: ensure no period where node targets are used without cert SANs, and automatic poison of delegated private hosted zone entries on rollbacks.

maria (support): closing loop with customer. If anything else pops up I'll re-open. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
